prompt:
Four animation frames of one effect for a 2D side-view game, painted side by side on one wide flat green field: the red double beat pulse of a Keeper's chest clock. Only the effect is drawn, no clock face and no creature. The four frames stand in one row on the same horizontal centre line, centres at exactly one eighth, three eighths, five eighths and seven eighths of the picture width, evenly spaced, never touching each other or the edge. Flat, face-on, seen at game-sprite distance; the largest frame spans about a fifth of the picture width.

The look is the glowing red shot of a dark etched storybook game: a hot, near-white cream core #FFF5DC, then a bright crimson #FF3658 body, a coral #FF7848 inner edge, and a deep shadow red #8F173C on the lower edge, with fine etched hatching in the shadow and a thin near-black ink edge #171614. A soft crimson glow hugs each shape but stays inside a short distance of it. A few tiny ember sparks float around.

Frame 1 (hand begins to glow): a short thick curved arc of crimson, a quarter of a circle, with a bright cream-hot head at its leading end and a few embers. Frame 2 (first beat): the arc has swept to three quarters of a circle, a bright glowing red ring segment with a white-hot head, and a small sharp starburst flash of coral at the head. Frame 3 (second beat): the full circle is closed, two thin crimson rings, one inside the other, with a second smaller coral starburst flash at the top and sharp ember shards flying out. Frame 4 (fade): the rings are broken into dim crimson dashes and a few drifting embers, the faintest frame.

Each shape is fully opaque with painted glow, no see-through colour. Colours only: crimson #FF3658, coral #FF7848, shadow red #8F173C, cream #FFF5DC, ink #171614. Outside the shapes the picture is one perfectly flat, pure green #00FF00 filling the canvas. No text, labels, grid, frames or watermark.
